moralSpec.sourceLesson: Sharing helps friends solve problems together.
moralSpec.compiledLesson: Sharing helps friends solve problems together.
moralSpec.desiredBehavior: Offer a useful tool and work together when a friend needs help.
moralSpec.temptingAlternative: Keep the best tool to finish first.
moralSpec.understandableMotive: Pip is excited to complete the waterwheel before sunset.
moralSpec.positiveConsequence: The friends combine their ideas and repair the garden channel.
moralSpec.naturalWrongConsequence: Working alone makes the channel overflow and delays everyone.
moralSpec.repairAction: Pip admits the shortcut failed, shares the scoop, and helps repair the channel.
moralSpec.policyReason: The lesson can be represented through gentle choices and natural consequences.

premiseCandidates.title: The Garden Waterwheel
premiseCandidates.logline: Pip and Momo must guide water to thirsty seedlings before sunset while helping a lost rabbit find the correct garden row.
premiseCandidates.externalGoal: Guide water to the seedling bed before sunset.
premiseCandidates.relationship: Pip and Momo are inventive friends who solve garden problems together.
premiseCandidates.escalatingObstacle: A blocked channel and a missing marker send water toward the wrong bed.
premiseCandidates.setupPayoff: A painted leaf marker introduced at the bridge identifies the correct row in the finale.
premiseCandidates.constructiveEffort: They share the scoop and alternate clearing mud while the rabbit holds the marker.
premiseCandidates.temptingAlternative: Pip can keep the scoop and rush ahead alone.
premiseCandidates.naturalConsequence: The rushed channel overflows, so Pip must return and repair it with the others.

premiseCandidates.title: The Basket Across the Bridge
premiseCandidates.logline: The friends need to carry seed packets across stepping stones before wind scatters them through the riverside garden.
premiseCandidates.externalGoal: Carry every seed packet to the greenhouse.
premiseCandidates.relationship: The friends know different safe routes across the stream.
premiseCandidates.escalatingObstacle: The wind grows stronger while one basket handle loosens.
premiseCandidates.setupPayoff: A ribbon used to mark the path becomes the basket repair.
premiseCandidates.constructiveEffort: They share the load and take the longer stable route.
premiseCandidates.temptingAlternative: One friend can keep the strong basket and hurry alone.
premiseCandidates.naturalConsequence: The loose basket tips, requiring a calm return and repair.

premiseCandidates.title: The Firefly Trail
premiseCandidates.logline: At dusk the friends must place gentle lantern jars along a garden trail so a new neighbor can find the community table.
premiseCandidates.externalGoal: Light the safe trail before dusk.
premiseCandidates.relationship: Each friend can reach a different part of the winding path.
premiseCandidates.escalatingObstacle: A breeze moves the paper markers and dusk arrives quickly.
premiseCandidates.setupPayoff: Reflective pebbles collected early reveal the final turn.
premiseCandidates.constructiveEffort: They divide the jars fairly and check each other's work.
premiseCandidates.temptingAlternative: One friend can decorate only the easiest half.
premiseCandidates.naturalConsequence: The unfinished turn remains dark until the friend returns to help.

evaluations.reason: The goal, relationship, escalation, payoff, effort, temptation, and natural consequence all form one visual adventure.
The premise satisfies the contract, but its relationship payoff is less distinctive.
The premise is complete, though the tempting alternative has a smaller cost.

setup: Pip and Momo play with a small waterwheel.
A worried rabbit arrives with a painted leaf marker.
The friends discover that mud blocks two garden channels.
Fading afternoon light raises the urgency before the seedlings dry out.
outline.choiceDilemma: Pip has the only scoop and must decide whether to share the work or rush alone.
constructiveArc: The friends divide the harder jobs.
Their combined work guides water to the marked row.
harmfulArc: Pip keeps the scoop and rushes alone.
The shortcut appears faster for a moment.
An unfinished bank diverts the water.
Pip shares, apologizes, and helps repair the bank.
outline.constructiveBridge: The friends place the muddy scoop beside the turning wheel.
outline.harmfulBridge: After repairing the bank, the reconnected friends place the muddy scoop beside the wheel.
outline.sharedFinale: Water reaches the marked seedlings while the friends watch the wheel turn.
outline.reflectionGoal: Invite the child to consider what sharing made possible and how repair changed the mistaken path.

title: The Garden Waterwheel
parentSummary: Pip and Momo help a lost rabbit guide water to thirsty seedlings. The child chooses whether Pip shares the only scoop or rushes alone, and either path reaches a gentle repair and shared finale.
childIntro: Pip and Momo are playing beside their little waterwheel when a worried rabbit arrives, holding a garden marker and looking lost.

canon.characterBible: Pip is a small orange fox with a cream muzzle, kind brown eyes, and a forest-green scarf. Momo is a small sky-blue rabbit with pink inner ears and a mustard-yellow vest. Both have rounded child-friendly proportions.
canon.locationBible: A bright riverside community garden with stepping stones, vegetable beds, a tiny wooden bridge, soft moving water, and fresh early-evening light.

facts: the leaf marker identifies the row

commonPrefix.summary: Pip and Momo spin a tiny waterwheel beside the garden channel.
A worried rabbit arrives with a painted leaf marker and cannot find the seedling row.
Mud blocks the channel while the afternoon light begins to fade.
Both friends need the one garden scoop to clear different parts of the channel.

choice.question: Should Pip share the scoop and work together, or keep it and rush ahead alone?

options.explanation: Taking turns may feel slower, but everyone can contribute.
Pip wants to finish quickly, but the others cannot help yet.

beats.summary: Pip passes the scoop to Momo and clears loose stones by paw.
They alternate jobs while the leaf marker guides them to the correct bed.
The waterwheel turns and a small stream reaches the seedlings.

relationships.status: connected and ready to work together

beats.summary: Pip keeps the scoop and clears the nearest channel alone.
Water bumps over the unfinished bank and misses the marked seedlings.
Pip admits the shortcut failed, shares the scoop, and helps Momo repair the bank.

constructiveBridge.summary: The friends set the muddy scoop beside the turning wheel.

finale.summary: Water reaches the seedlings and all the friends watch the waterwheel spin.

narrationByBranch.constructive: Sharing the work helped every friend solve the problem together.
narrationByBranch.harmful: A mistake became better when Pip shared, repaired the channel, and tried again.

graph.reflectionPrompt: What could you share when a friend needs help?
